source.title: In-Context Collapse in Vision-Language Models and How to Mitigate it?

page_placements.theme: Label-copying heads in few-shot classification ICL, and the failure modes they cause

record.tranche_reason: The paper discusses text-only induction heads as background, but its experiments measure image–label in-context behavior in vision-language models, not induction heads or their formation. Its results therefore do not test the listed claim versions.
record.gate_note: The paper mentions induction heads in Related Work, citing them as a text-only circuit for repeated-pattern completion. Its own results concern multimodal image–label ICL, including recency copying, collapse, and interventions at VLM integration layers; none measures the specified induction-head mechanism, training-time formation, or a loss-curve transition. The related VLM findings are recorded under fits_no_version.
record.test_reason: Induction heads appear only in one Related Work sentence citing Olsson et al. The experiments measure image–label ICL accuracy, recency copy rate, and LoRA locus rescue in VLMs. No head-level attention analysis, no training dynamics, and no token-index loss are reported, so no version is tested.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors conclude that many-shot VLM ICL can collapse, sometimes below chance. They find robustness to added demonstrations and novel-rule learning are dissociable. The collapse is causally localized to the connector and early/mid layers and can be repaired by a transferable integration-locus adapter. The late layers are instead best for continual consolidation. The paper makes no induction-head claims.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses image–label prompts and VLM integration-locus interventions, rather than measuring or intervening on induction heads in small attention-only transformers.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported multimodal collapse varies by model, task, and label condition; the paper reports standard-label collapse and remap-learning results separately.

fits_no_version.finding: In several VLMs, adding correctly labelled image–label demonstrations lowers standard accuracy. Lost predictions track the most recent demonstration's label (e.g. Qwen2-VL-2B CIFAR-4: 0.94→0.44 accuracy; copy rate 0→0.83 at K=1). Shuffled labels give about the same accuracy as standard labels.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Many-shot multimodal ICL can collapse through a recency-copy heuristic. This is a behavioural phenomenon distinct from token-level induction-head copying.

fits_no_version.finding: Remap (arbitrary-label) learning stays near chance in collapse-prone VLMs. It rises in Qwen2-VL-7B and Qwen2.5-VL-7B (e.g. CIFAR remap 0.32→0.80). LoRA on connector/early layers restores it (shapes 0.39→0.91/0.96); a late-layer adapter does not (0.08).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Novel-rule multimodal ICL depends on capacity at the vision–language integration layers rather than the readout layers.

record.problems: The study's evidence is not about induction heads or their formation. The recorded multimodal results use a limited set of image–label tasks and do not provide a direct measurement of the claim's token-level behavior.
record.rows_left_out: Other VLM collapse, intervention, vaccine, and continual-learning results were left out because they do not measure induction-head behavior or the specific versions of the claim.

untested.parts: No circuit analysis of previous-token or induction heads.
No training-time measurements; all models are frozen pretrained checkpoints.
No attribution of ICL to induction heads; no loss-by-token-index measure.
No search for induction-behaviour heads in VLMs or other modalities.
No variation of training data or setup affecting head formation. Alignment-recipe effects are asserted, but not on induction heads.
No comparison of induction heads against other heads for few-shot learning.

record.verdict_notes: Relation changed from 'discusses' to 'cites_only'. The paper mentions induction heads once as background and offers no argument about any version. The recency-copy finding might seem superficially related to induction-style copying, but it is behavioural and at the image–label level, with no head analysis.

versions.untested_parts: No test of induction heads composing with previous-token heads or implementing the specified token-copying pattern.
No induction-head formation measurements, training-time sweep, ICL loss-by-token-index measure, or training-loss curve.
No test of induction heads as the mechanism behind most in-context learning in large transformers.
The study evaluates VLMs but does not measure whether they contain heads with induction behavior; it also does not test other architectures or modalities for such heads.
The study varies tasks and models for multimodal ICL collapse, but does not test whether induction-head formation or its timing depends on data or training setup.
No test of induction heads as the carrier of few-shot task learning versus other heads or mechanisms.
No analysis of induction-head formation sub-steps or multiple training transitions.
